You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From f90d6126eda6b344baed8e5c628179ed2b02be48 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Derek Bruening <bruening@google.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2015 12:38:55 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] i#1686 decoder tests: OP_mov and OP_lsl do not touch flags

Fixes a bug from 4d8bc7cf2f799ffe0434f9fa59186efe988b5400: OP_mov and
OP_lsl do not touch the condition flags.

Also fixes a release-build compiler warning with recent gcc versions.

Review-URL: https://codereview.appspot.com/229330043
---
 core/arch/arm/disassemble.c     | 2 +-
 core/arch/arm/table_t32_16_it.c | 4 ++--
 2 files changed, 3 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/core/arch/arm/disassemble.c b/core/arch/arm/disassemble.c
index 59034f57a..bbd7f7874 100644
--- a/core/arch/arm/disassemble.c
+++ b/core/arch/arm/disassemble.c
@@ -356,7 +356,7 @@ opnd_disassemble_noimplicit(char *buf, size_t bufsz, size_t *sofar INOUT,
         bool writeback;
         if (reads_list)
             memop = opnd;
-        if (writes_list)
+        else
             memop = instr_get_src(instr, 0);
         CLIENT_ASSERT(opnd_is_base_disp(memop), "internal disasm error");
         last = instr_get_dst(instr, instr_num_dsts(instr) - 1);
diff --git a/core/arch/arm/table_t32_16_it.c b/core/arch/arm/table_t32_16_it.c
index b626d5dfe..9d73cd9c1 100644
--- a/core/arch/arm/table_t32_16_it.c
+++ b/core/arch/arm/table_t32_16_it.c
@@ -276,7 +276,7 @@ const instr_info_t T32_16_it_ext_bits_6_4[][8] = {
 const instr_info_t T32_16_it_ext_imm_10_6[][2] = {
     /* {op/type, op encoding, name, dst1, dst2, src1, src2, src3, flags, eflags, code} */
     { /* 0 */
-      {OP_mov,   0x0000, "mov",        RZw, xx, RYw,   xx, xx, no, fWNZCV, z96[1][0x08]},
-      {OP_lsl,   0x0000, "lsl",        RZw, xx, RYw, i5_6, xx, no, fWNZCV, z96[0][0x02]},
+      {OP_mov,   0x0000, "mov",        RZw, xx, RYw,   xx, xx, no, x, z96[1][0x08]},
+      {OP_lsl,   0x0000, "lsl",        RZw, xx, RYw, i5_6, xx, no, x, z96[0][0x02]},
     },
 };
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the condition flags for the ARM instructions OP_mov and OP_lsl. These instructions were previously marked as affecting the flags (fWNZCV), but they do not actually modify the condition flags in the ARM architecture. The patch corrects this by changing the flags to 'x', indicating that these operations do not affect the flags, thus fixing the disassembly and ensuring accurate instruction representation.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>
    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the condition flags for the ARM instructions OP_mov and OP_lsl. These instructions were previously marked as affecting the flags (fWNZCV), but they do not actually modify the condition flags in the ARM architecture. The patch corrects this by changing the flags to 'x', indicating that these operations do not affect the flags, thus fixing the disassembly and ensuring accurate instruction representation.
